messages.subject: multiple data sets
messages.body_plain:
Is it possible to analyze multiple data sets with R/qtl (such as
combining two F2 data sets or two backcross data sets)?  If so, what is
the best way to do this?
messages.body_snippet:
Is it possible to analyze multiple data sets with R/qtl (such as
combining two F2 data sets or two backcross data sets)?  If so, what is
the best way to do this?

messages.subject: Re: multiple data sets
messages.body_plain:
There's no automatic way to do this, and I certainly wouldn't
want to say that I know what the best way to do it is.

One approach is to get the maps lined up exactly, and combine
the two crosses into one, but with a covariate indicating which
cross an individual is from, and then doing the QTL analysis with
that covariate included in the model.

regards,
karl

messages.subject: combining crosses
messages.body_plain:
Is it possible to combine crosses that do not have the exact same
genetic map? (such as two crosses that used different markers)
messages.body_snippet:
Is it possible to combine crosses that do not have the exact same

messages.subject: Re: combining crosses
messages.body_plain:
You would need to create a map that included all of the markers,
though some could be typed in one cross but not the other.

karl

messages.subject: subsetting individual chromosomes
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am new to R/QTL and have imported data from QTL Cartographer into R.
My chromosomes were named chr-1, chr-2,...,chr-5 in my original files
but were renamed by R to be:

levels(numleavout.em$chr)
[1] "-1" "-2" "-3" "-4" "-5"

when I try to plot my LOD scores one chromosome at a time, I get the
following error:

 plot(numleavout.em,chr=-1)
Error in plot.scanone(numleavout.em, chr = -1) :
        Chromosome(s) to plot were not matched to those in the scanone
output.

The plot error suggests I am using the wrong chromosome names but the
levels output suggests I am using the correct chromosome names.  How
should I be subsetting the individual chromosomes?

Thanks

messages.subject: Re: subsetting individual chromosomes
messages.body_plain:
Yes, things are looking a little strange.
It's best to call the chromosomes "1", "2", etc.
"chr1", "chr2", etc. should work, but "chr-1", "chr-2" seem
to reveal a bug.

I think in reading in the data, we look for things like "chr1",
"chr2" and then strip off the "chr" part.  But if they're labeled
"chr-1" then end up being labelled with negative numbers, which
causes problems later on, as in subsetting, you can generally use
-1 to mean plotting all chromosomes *except* chr 1.

If you go into your cartographer files and replace things like
"chr-1" with "chr1", everything should work.

And in future versions, hopefully I'll remember to fix this.

karl

messages.subject: running out of memeory while using SCANTWO
messages.subject_clean: running out of memeory while using SCANTWO
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

This may be more of an R question, but it comes up while using scantwo,
so here goes.  I am getting error message indicating R is running out
of memory:

1: Reached total allocation of 767Mb: see help(memory.size)
2: Reached total allocation of 767Mb: see help(memory.size)

I have increased the virtual memory used by Windows (1152-4000mb) and
set the memory size as large as R will let me:

> memory.limit(size=4000)

Now when I run scantwo, I get errors like the following:

Error: cannot allocate vector of size 66560 Kb

I am running Windows XP on a P4 3.2Ghz laptop with 768MB ram.  My
dataset has N=640, 243 markers on 5 chromosomes, 1 phenotype and 1
additive covariate, and I imputed pseudomarkers on 256 pages at 2cM
intervals.  I am using method="imp" for scantwo.  When I do MIM on QTL
cartographer, my computer handles this dataset fine and takes somewhere
between 12-20 hrs to analyze.

How can I get R/qtl to analyze my data?  Is there any way to increase
R's memory limits?

Thank you

Tarek

messages.subject: Re: running out of memeory while using SCANTWO
messages.subject_clean: running out of memeory while using SCANTWO
messages.body_plain:
You're running out of memory.  The 256 imputations take a lot
of memory, especially at 2 cM resolution.

Your options are: use the "em" method rather than imputation
("em" is equivalent to MIM in QTL Cartographer.); do fewer
imputations; use a bigger step size; or get a computer with
more RAM.

karl
